summary: San Cristóbal Airport is the main air gateway to the eastern Galápagos Islands, located on San Cristóbal Island and serving the provincial capital of Puerto Baquerizo Moreno. The small terminal handles both domestic flights from mainland Ecuador and inter-island connections to other islands in the archipelago. Its proximity to town and the surrounding wildlife-rich coastline make it a distinctive entry point to one of the world's most celebrated natural destinations.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate at San Cristóbal Airport?
A: The airport is served primarily by local carriers providing flights from Guayaquil and Quito on mainland Ecuador, as well as inter-island flights connecting to other Galápagos islands like Isabela.

Q: Is there a departure tax or entrance fee for the Galápagos?
A: Yes, visitors to the Galápagos must pay a national park entrance fee and a separate transit control card fee, which is typically collected before arrival.

Q: How far is the airport from Puerto Baquerizo Moreno?
A: The airport is located just a few minutes from the town center, making it one of the most conveniently positioned airports in the Galápagos.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Rental options are limited; most visitors arrange pickups, taxis, or small-group transfers through their accommodations or tour operators.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged hotel transfers are the most common ways to reach Puerto Baquerizo Moreno from the airport, with the short journey taking only a few minutes. Many tour operators and hostels include airport pickup when booking multi-day Galápagos packages. Walking into town is also feasible for light travelers, as the terminal sits on the edge of the settlement.
local_tip: After landing, head to the nearby waterfront within walking distance of the terminal — you can often spot sea lions resting on benches and benches along the malecón, giving you a first taste of Galápagos wildlife before you even check into your hotel.
